preamble:
This module allows to define new -X options.

The functions below are intended to be used with partial application to define options at the top-level of a module:

  let discombobulate = bool ~loc:__LOC__ "discombobulate"

and used in code as if discombobulate () then ....

-X options can be passed on the command line as -X name=value.

Note: -X options are intended for internal use only. They are not documented in the output of --help and may be removed without notice.
content:
val string : loc:string -> string -> default:string -> unit -> string

string ~loc:__LOC__ name ~default defines a new extra option which accepts arbitrary strings.

val int : loc:string -> string -> default:int -> unit -> int

int ~loc:__LOC__ name ~default defines a new extra option which accepts only integers.

val bool : loc:string -> string -> unit -> bool

bool ~loc:__LOC__ name defines a new extra option which accepts booleans written as the integers '0' and '1'. In addition, -X name is equivalent to -X name=1.

Boolean options define a pair of options: name and no-name, which are inverses of each others.

val symbol : loc:string -> string -> default:'a -> (string * 'a) list -> unit -> 'a

symbol ~loc:__LOC__ name ~default spec defines a new extra option which accepts only the strings in spec and associates them with the corresponding value.

val parse_and_set : string -> (unit, string) Stdlib.result
